how: Loop format (Matteo 2026-11-17). One recording per reel. Each loop line = bridge + hook said in ONE breath; the edit starts the reel at the hook and ends it on the bridge, so the replay is the same continuous sentence. Edit here, then run build_loop.py.
intro: Fighter breakdown, episode {ep}. I'm Matteo. I've trained in five countries, and every episode I break down one fighter you can learn from.
cta: Comment PLAN and the fighter you want next, and I'll send you the plan for this one.

reels.title: Ciryl Gane
reels.why: Recent hype: stopped Alex Pereira (TKO, round 2, UFC Freedom 250 at the White House, June 14) and was reported to have fought at UFC 334 on Nov 14. Replaces Tyson.
reels.note: Plan NOT written yet (Claude writes it before this posts). Confirm: Muay Thai start, the Pereira result and the UFC 334 result. Part three describes his style in general, not one fight, so pick clips that show exactly that.

loops.hook: Most heavyweights stand and trade. Gane never does.
Why do the biggest hitters in the UFC keep missing Ciryl Gane?

loops.bridge: And that's the style behind it.
loops.hook: Ciryl Gane stopped Alex Pereira at the White House. Here's how he fights.
Gane's best weapon isn't his power. It's his distance.

loops.bridge: It all starts with where he came from.
loops.hook: Ciryl Gane started in Muay Thai, and you can see it in his feet.

body: He's a heavyweight who moves like a lightweight, and it comes down to three things.
One. He never stands in front of you. A step to the side after every exchange, so your best shot hits air.
Two. His reach. A long jab and a teep from the edge of range, and he's gone before you can answer.
The third one is why big hitters struggle against him.
Three. He counters when you commit. Every time you step in with something big, he has already moved, and the counter lands on your way out.
So if you spar bigger hitters, don't stand in front of them. Step off the line, then answer.

reels.title: Justin Gaethje
reels.tag: Episode 5 · MMA · leg kicks and pressure
reels.why: Recent hype: stopped the undefeated Ilia Topuria (TKO, round 4) at UFC Freedom 250 on June 14 to become lightweight champion.
reels.note: Plan NOT written yet (Claude writes it before this posts). Confirm: the Topuria result, college wrestling background. Parts one to three describe his general style, so pick clips of his leg kicks and body work.

loops.hook: Gaethje doesn't out-skill you. He out-lasts you.
How did Gaethje beat an undefeated champion?
Gaethje stopped Ilia Topuria at the White House.
Gaethje isn't just a brawler. Look at what he does to your legs.

loops.bridge: It goes back to his past.
loops.hook: Gaethje was a college wrestler before he fought, and it shows in how calm he is under pressure.

body: He's a brawler with a plan, and it comes down to three things.
One. The leg kicks. Every round he chops at your lead leg, so your movement fades as the fight goes on.
Two. He walks forward without panic. He's fine taking one to give one, so you start fighting scared of the exchange.
The third one is what beat an undefeated champion.
Three. He makes every round cost you. The leg kicks and body shots take your speed, and once your hands slow down, the head shots land.
So if you're the one pressing, make your partner pay in the legs and the body first. The head comes later.

reels.title: Naoya Inoue
reels.tag: Episode 6 · Boxing · balance and body shots
reels.why: Recent hype: beat Junto Nakatani by decision at the Tokyo Dome on May 2 (about 55,000 fans) to stay undefeated at 33 and 0 and keep the undisputed super bantamweight title.
reels.note: Plan NOT written yet (Claude writes it before this posts). Confirm: 33 and 0, five foot five, learned boxing from his father. Part three (balance) is a style breakdown, so check it against a clip.

loops.hook: Everyone talks about Inoue's power. Watch his feet instead.
How does a five-foot-five super bantamweight hit this hard?
Thirty-three fights, zero losses, and a sold-out Tokyo Dome. Here's what Inoue does.
Inoue's nickname is the Monster. His real weapon is his balance.

loops.bridge: It goes back to when he was a kid.
loops.hook: Inoue learned boxing from his father as a kid, and he still fights on the basics.

body: He's called the Monster, and it comes down to three things.
One. The jab. Fast, from the edge of range. It measures you and hides everything behind it.
Two. The body shot. He digs to the body early, so your guard comes down by the middle rounds.
The third one is why his power looks so heavy.
Three. Balance. His weight is over his feet on every punch, so the whole body goes into it, even the ones that don't look big.
So if you want more power, don't swing harder. Get your feet under you first.

reels.title: Alex Pereira
reels.tag: Episode 7 · Kickboxing in MMA · the left hook (optional 4th)
reels.why: Recent hype, mixed: stopped by Ciryl Gane (round 2) on June 14. Still the biggest name in kickboxing-to-MMA, and the left hook is a classic breakdown. Skip it if you want only winners.
reels.note: Plan NOT written yet (Claude writes it before this posts). Confirm: Glory kickboxing champion, UFC champion in two weight classes. Parts are his general setup, so pick clips that show leg kick then hook.

loops.hook: Pereira doesn't throw the left hook to land it. He throws kicks so it lands.
Why does Alex Pereira's left hook land even when you know it's coming?
Pereira was champion in two weight classes. Here's the weapon behind it.
Pereira's best weapon isn't the left hook. It's the leg kick.

loops.bridge: It all goes back to kickboxing.
loops.hook: Pereira was a kickboxing champion before he ever fought in the UFC.

body: His left hook is famous, and it comes down to three things.
One. The leg kicks. He chops at your legs, so your hands drop to check them.
Two. The patience. He stays loose and relaxed, waiting for the exact moment you look down.
The third one is the one that ends fights.
Three. The left hook over the top. It comes with his whole body behind it, right into the space the kick just opened.
So if you throw a hook, set it up. Kick low first, then go high.
